alex: Quick sync — prototype for the "rollback operators" landed. Idea: represent canary/A-B rollout + automatic fallback with three small primitives: Gate (traffic slicing), Probe (signals/health), Operator (action executor). Thoughts?

samira: Really like separating concerns. Main Q: where does the authoritative state live? local edge node vs central coordinator? ops needs deterministic fast reaction (<200ms) for bad-model scenarios.

keith: Centralized gives a global picture (cross-region), but adds reaction latency and single point of slowdowns. Can we do a hybrid: Gate runs in the local router, Probe emits local metrics and forwards summaries to central, and Operator decisions come from a local policy engine with a central override path?

lina: Hybrid sounds pragmatic. We need a simple central->local override API: `POST /agent/v1/override {policy_id, expires_at, reason}` and a lease model so overrides expire if the control plane loses connectivity.

alex: Agreed. Also, operators must be safe: idempotent actions and a `revert-token` returned on apply, e.g. `{"op_id":"abc123","revert_token":"rT-...", "ttl_s":300}` so rollbacks are explicit and auditable.

ops-bot: deploybot: Canary rollout started for `search-v3` at 2026-03-23T14:30Z — initial slice 5% with ramp rules.

samira: A real tradeoff: local-only operators reduce blast radius but can cause divergence if two routers disagree on state. We should publish a versioned, signed policy manifest pushed to routers; caches validate signatures and fallback to last-known safe manifest.

keith: On the interface boundary: expose a tiny sync call `evaluate(policy_id, signal)` that returns `{action, confidence, op_hint}`. Keep the policy evaluation engine stateless so nodes can restart without heavy restore. Operators should persist minimal audit logs only.

lina: Long-term refactor idea: replace the ad-hoc Gate DSL with a typed policy language (a constrained subset of Rego or a tiny Rust-based DSL) so we can run static verification and unit tests on rollout rules.

alex: Good calls. Next steps: I'll open an RFC PR with architecture diagram, sequence flows for `apply`/`revert` and the `revert-token` lifecycle, plus the central override lease semantics. Will add a sample `operator` HTTP contract and TTL defaults.

samira: +1 — add a short test harness that simulates control-plane partitioning and split-brain where two routers diverge and later reconcile.

keith: +1 as well. One more: ensure Operators expose metrics like `operator_apply_latency` and `operator_conflicts_total` for alerting.

ops-bot: reaction :thumbsup:
